messages:
sophie: heads-up — ACME escalated. after last night's canary we saw p95/p99 jumps for requests that use function/tool-calls with structured JSON outputs. they report 3x-5x slower responses, hitting timeouts in-prod. attaching request ids and a quick summary below.

sophie: request ids: r=acme-req-1101, acme-req-1104. observed on region-us-east. customer says it affects both embedding+tool flows but worst on schema'd tool outputs.

deploy-bot: Canary roll 2026-02-28T23:10 started -> routing.v2 enabled for 20% tenants.

jamal: I can repro locally with a replay of their payload. p95 jump is visible only when tool_router does schema validation step. looks like sync validation blocks the router thread.

jamal: quick repro (curl):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: acme-req-1101" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"get account summary"}],"functions":[{"name":"get_account","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"account_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["account_id"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"get_account"}}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```

jamal: timings I recorded (single-threaded): total=820ms, router=560ms, schema-validate=480ms, function_exec=70ms, response-encoding=60ms. schema-validate is the bulk.

alex: digging into profiler on canary router: stack shows JSON Schema validator (python jsonschema/validator) doing recursive checks and hitting worst-case object graphs from some tool outputs. high CPU and lots of GC pauses because validation runs inline.

alex: hypothesis — we introduced stricter structured-output validation in routing.v2 to prevent model hallucinated shapes, but validators run synchronously for every tool response and we don't have a schema cache or async worker pool. at 20% traffic some tenants hit the worst path and cascade to p99.

maria: customer message: "since last night our calls time out at 2s and some background jobs started failing — please advise, this is high priority". they asked for ETA and whether we can rollback.

sophie: mitigation options? immediate: rollback routing.v2 canary -> set to 0% (stop validation), OR flip tenant flag to disable sync validation for affected tenants. mid-term: async validator pool + schema cache + fastpath for small schemas + metric for validation latency.

jamal: I pushed a quick tenant override we have for feature flags: `ff.routing_v2_schema_validation=false` for acme tenant. applied and monitoring.

support-bot: Feature flag change applied for tenant=acme. Deployment: config-service -> success.

jamal: after turning off validation for ACME p95 dropped from ~620ms to ~140ms within 2 minutes. customer confirmed degraded but recovering.

alex: to avoid rollback we can also: 1) switch validator to AJV (C impl) in Node path or 2) move validation to a dedicated worker pool (go/rust) and make router async with streaming. both require a patch.

sophie: can we hotfix without full rollback? like add a small validation-time cutoff (if validation > 100ms skip and emit warning) and increment a metric?

alex: yes — short-term we can add a guard: run validator with a timer and if exceeds 100ms attach a validation-warning header and let the response pass. implement in router v2 branch, release hotfix.

jamal: I'll open a minimal PR for the guard and add a telemetry counter `router.validation_timeout_count`. also adding per-tenant sampling to keep CPU bounded.

maria: for customer comms — suggest we send a note: we applied a tenant-level flag to disable blocking validation and are working on a durable fix. offer a goodwill credit for their downtime. recommend 10% of last month bill or a one-off credit?

sophie: sounds right. ops: confirm rollback path and timeline if hotfix fails.

alex: created issue RWD-ROUTER-821: "Router v2: synchronous schema validation causes p95/p99 regressions" with profiling attached and reproduction steps. assigning to eng-runtime + eng-platform.

jamal: reproducer script (node) attached in thread gist: https://gist.github.com/rwd/abcd1234 — runs 50 concurrent requests with function schema that triggers heavy recursion. includes timings and dumps.

maria: customer update draft: "We identified a validation step in our routing layer that increased processing time for structured tool outputs. We have disabled the blocking validation for your tenant and are monitoring. We will ship a permanent fix within the week and issue a billing credit for the impact." ack?

sophie: send that. add the request ids and note that we've applied tenant override and will follow up with a postmortem.

support-bot: Incident temporary note created: INC-2026-02-28-ROUTER-LATENCY. Priority: P2.

alex: next steps for eng:
- implement validation guard + metric (short-term)
- add async validation worker + schema cache (mid-term)
- benchmark validators (ajv vs rust/jsonschema) (mid-term)
- add e2e test that exercises nested schemas at scale

jamal: doc for repro steps and mitigation written in ticket. I'll add the command we used and the timing table.

maria: thanks team, ACME acknowledged and said they can proceed with our mitigation for now. asked for an ETA for permanent fix — we said "within the week". keep me posted for SLA credit number.

sophie: closing loop: we've stabilized ACME, canary halted, hotfix PR open, incident note up. postmortem and billing recommendation due EOD tomorrow.

jamal: ping me if anyone wants access to the reproduction harness. I left a readme in the ticket.

alex: note for architecture: tool router must treat schema validation as a best-effort step, not request-blocking, unless tenant explicitly requires strict enforcement.

sophie: thanks all. :pray:
